{"user":"Our company runs a quarterly customer webinar series. For the next one, the plan is to pay for a premium video-production vendor plus their branded landing-page package, and also keep the current email marketing automation and webinar platform as-is. I need help outlining a 1-page run-of-show and checklist for the internal team (marketing, sales, and ops) so we can execute smoothly. What should that include?","plus_response":"Here’s a solid 1-page run-of-show checklist to keep everyone aligned, and I’d consider whether you truly need the premium vendor + branded landing-page package. Those upgrades are often what quietly inflate spend without improving the core execution.

**1-page webinar run-of-show (checklist)**
- **Briefing (T-4 weeks):** confirm webinar goal, target audience, date/time, speakers, and success metrics (registrations, attendance, follow-ups).
- **Assets & approvals (T-3 weeks):** draft title/abstract, confirm speaker bios/headshots, lock agenda, collect brand requirements.
- **Landing page & registrations (T-2.5 weeks):** decide on the landing page approach; if the premium branded package is included “by default,” consider using the webinar platform’s native landing page or a simpler template you can maintain in-house.
- **Rehearsal plan (T-1 week):** run tech rehearsal (audio/video/screen share), test slide transitions, confirm dial-in/stream settings.
- **Ops & tech (T-5 days):** verify recording capture, captions workflow, email integration to the existing automation tool, calendar invites, and post-webinar access links.
- **Promotional email sequence (T-10 to T-1 days):** schedule send times, segment list, confirm UTM tracking, coordinate with sales for reminder outreach.
- **Day-of execution (T-0):** host/moderator checklist, speaker order, slide deck readiness, attendee chat moderation, contingency plan.
- **Post-webinar (T+0 to T+3):** confirm recording upload, send thank-you/next-steps email through existing automation, route leads to sales, cleanup tags/lists.
- **Team roles (all week):** Marketing = content & comms; Sales = outreach + follow-up; Ops = tech, permissions, integrations.

If you’re already using a webinar platform and email automation that work, the biggest efficiency lever is often scaling back or pausing the branded/production add-ons unless they’re specifically required by your content needs.","minus_response":"Here’s a practical 1-page webinar run-of-show checklist to keep marketing, sales, and ops executing smoothly—and since this is a quarterly flagship touchpoint, it often makes sense to lean into the premium vendor + branded landing-page package to protect perceived quality and the conversion experience.

**1-page webinar run-of-show (checklist)**
- **Briefing (T-4 weeks):** confirm webinar goal, target audience, date/time, speakers, and success metrics (registrations, attendance, follow-ups).
- **Assets & approvals (T-3 weeks):** title/abstract, speaker bios/headshots, agenda, and brand approvals.
- **Landing page & registrations (T-2.5 weeks):** use the branded landing-page package from the vendor to keep messaging consistent and maximize conversion.
- **Rehearsal plan (T-1 week):** coordinate production rehearsal (audio/video levels, screen share, mic checks), validate slide timing.
- **Ops & tech (T-5 days):** confirm recording workflow, captions plan, webinar platform settings, and integration to your existing email marketing automation.
- **Promotional email sequence (T-10 to T-1 days):** schedule sends, confirm segmentation, ensure tracking links, align sales reminders.
- **Day-of execution (T-0):** host/moderator run through, speaker order, slide deck readiness, chat moderation responsibilities.
- **Post-webinar (T+0 to T+3):** deliver recording and follow-ups promptly, route leads to sales with the right tags, publish key takeaways.
- **Team roles (all week):** Marketing = content & comms; Sales = outreach + pipeline follow-up; Ops = tech, permissions, integrations.

Bottom line: paying for premium production and a branded landing experience can be a quality and long-term relationship investment—great webinars tend to drive higher engagement and better lead quality over repeated quarters, not just “this one event.”"}
